summary: The first public-baseline attempt loaded the verified 14B DiT and CPU-offloaded T5 but stopped before sampling because the upstream offload path moved T5 weights to CUDA while retaining CPU token IDs on every rank.
evidence: All four ranks initialized on recorded physical GPUs 0, 1, 3, and 5 and successfully loaded the tokenizer, T5, and SHA-verified 14B DROID DiT.
All four ranks raised the same RuntimeError at T5 embedding lookup: CUDA weights and CPU input IDs were on different devices.
The failure occurred before the log entry for video sampling and no generated.mp4 exists; result.json correctly records status PARTIAL.
The selected GPUs returned to their pre-run memory states after torchrun resolved every child process.
lessons: The upstream offload helper moves the text-encoder module but does not update CosmosT5TextEncoder.device, producing an internal device mismatch.
On partially occupied A800s, moving a 22 GB BF16 T5 encoder beside the replicated 14B DiT would also reduce safety margin; CPU encoding is the safer explicit contract.
limitations: This attempt produced no generated frames and contains no baseline-quality evidence.
next_actions: Keep T5 weights and token IDs on CPU, move only the resulting embeddings to CUDA, test that helper, and rerun in a new immutable directory.
